record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: For commuting measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ and bounded measurable f0, ..., fℓ, does every correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ dμ admit a decomposition ψ(n) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro mean of |e(n)| tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Is it true that one always has a decomposition ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · . . . · T`^n f` dµ = ψ(n) + e(n) where (ψ(n)) is an `-step nilsequence and limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 |e(n)| = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T_1,\dots,T_\ell\colon X\to X$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations. For bounded measurable functions $f_0,f_1,\dots,f_\ell\colon X\to\mathbb{C}$, define the multi-correlation sequence
$$a(n)=\int_X f_0(x)\,f_1(T_1^n x)\,f_2(T_2^n x)\cdots f_\ell(T_\ell^n x)\,d\mu(x),\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.$$
An $\ell$-step nilsequence is a sequence of the form $\psi(n)=F(g^n\cdot e_\Gamma)$, where $G/\Gamma$ is an $\ell$-step nilmanifold ($G$ a connected, simply connected $\ell$-step nilpotent Lie group and $\Gamma$ a cocompact discrete subgroup), $g\in G$, and $F\colon G/\Gamma\to\mathbb{C}$ is continuous.

Question: For every choice of commuting measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T_1,\dots,T_\ell)$ and bounded measurable $f_0,\dots,f_\ell$, does the sequence $a(n)$ admit a decomposition
$$a(n)=\psi(n)+e(n)\qquad(n\in\mathbb{N})$$
where $\psi$ is an $\ell$-step nilsequence and $\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N |e(n)|=0$?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress is known: for actions of a single transformation along polynomial iterates, the decomposition was established by Frantzikinakis (2014). For commuting transformations, decompositions have been obtained in special settings (e.g., along primes, and for pairwise independent polynomial iterates). A 2025 preprint announces a proof that every multi-correlation sequence equals a generalized nilsequence plus a null-sequence, resolving a conjecture of Frantzikinakis in that form; however, whether the structured part can always be taken to be an honest ℓ-step nilsequence (rather than a generalized one) in the commuting setup, as originally stated, does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Multiple correlation sequences and nilsequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the structure of multiple correlation sequences defined by measure preserving actions of commuting transformations; when the iterates are integer polynomials, any such correlation sequence is the sum of a nilsequence and an error term small in uniform density.
status_evidence.claim: Single-transformation polynomial case and various commuting cases established.

status_evidence.title: A decomposition of multicorrelation sequences for commuting transformations along primes
status_evidence.snippet: Decomposition of multicorrelation sequences for commuting transformations along prime subsequences.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result along primes for commuting transformations.

status_evidence.title: Structured extensions and multi-correlation sequences
status_evidence.snippet: We show that every multi-correlation sequence is the sum of a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence. This proves a conjecture of N. Frantzikinakis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work resolves the conjecture in a generalized-nilsequence form.
